cells.tense: Something has started moving in you and you are letting it move at its own pace; you are not steering it ahead or holding it back.
cells.ask: Let one warm feeling reach you today and leave it unnamed for an hour — this keeps what you see from settling into something fixed.
cells.core:
On a good day here, you walk into a room and feel its weather — who is carrying something heavy, where the ease has shifted — and you take it in before you say anything about it. Being part of a conversation and seeing its whole shape at once is the thing you do, and people can usually tell you are paying attention.

Holding something open is not the easy position. You are letting a feeling arrive without deciding what it is yet, which leaves you without the relief of a conclusion, and sitting with it a while is what keeps what you notice from closing early. There is more of this to know.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the room and you leave the call open.
cells.verb: letting what is already here land in you before you name it
cells.place: standing where you can see the whole shape and still stand inside it

cells.tense: You are already seeing where this lands and how it turns out, so none of it can arrive at the speed it is actually moving.
cells.ask: Spend ten minutes with one thing you have decided is done, and let it be done — this gives you a finished piece instead of another check.
cells.core:
There are days when you take in how something is going and the next step comes on its own, without reaching for it. You see the shape and you move, and the people around you follow that call because it usually holds.

Lately you have been ahead of the moment you are actually in. The person is still talking and their ending is already decided; the day is still going and how it closes is already settled. Taking your next step from what is really in front of you, instead of from your own read of how it will land, is the way back — and it means giving up the comfort of getting there first.

cells.tense: You are watching what is happening around you instead of standing in it, and the watching has gone quiet on you.
cells.ask: Say one thing about what you notice here, out loud, plainly — this puts your own voice back in the room.
cells.core:
You can be part of a conversation and also outside it — hearing the whole thing while you are inside it. That double view is yours, and it means you rarely miss what is going on, and people feel you are with them while you take them in.

What is missing right now is the landing. Things are happening around you and you are taking them in from a distance, without any of it reaching you, and saying one plain thing about where you are puts your own part back into the room. Walking away still works; this is a small step, taken in daylight, in a room you are already in.

cells.tense: You already see the shape of what is happening here and you are talking about it as if it arrived from somewhere else.
cells.ask: Say out loud once that a read you got — the accurate one you acted on — was yours, not the situation's.
cells.core:
When you say the shape of a thing — that it was going to go this way, that someone had already left — you are usually right, and people have learned to trust the call. The accuracy has not been in question.

What gets left off the table is who did the reading. You credit the situation, the timing, what was obvious to anyone. Naming it as yours takes it out of the air and puts it back where it came from — and it stays exactly as true. The cost is standing behind your own words for a minute.
cells.sheetLine: You called it, and you are still saying it wasn't you.
